questions.prompt: A navigation receives an HTTP redirect before the HTML response. What should the loading trace show?

choices.text: Commit the redirect as the final document before requesting its target.
A follow-up request to the redirect target before the document is committed.
Wait for the redirected page load event before requesting the redirect target.
Follow the redirect only if page JavaScript explicitly assigns the target URL.

questions.explanation: Navigation follows the redirect destination before committing a suitable final document. It does not require page JavaScript or a load event for the destination first.

sources.title: Inside look at modern web browser (part 2)
sources.claim: Navigation uses network requests, may follow redirects, checks response type and commits the document to a renderer.

questions.prompt: Two external classic scripts use `defer` in document order. What behavior can their author rely on?

choices.text: They execute after parsing in their document order.
They execute as downloads finish, regardless of their document order.
They block parsing at each script tag until that download completes.
They execute only after every image and video resource has loaded.

questions.explanation: Deferred classic scripts wait for parsing and retain document order. Async scripts instead execute when ready; defer does not mean waiting for every image.

sources.title: HTML Standard: scripting
sources.claim: Classic script execution depends on async and defer; module scripts are deferred by default and async changes their scheduling.

questions.prompt: A browser parses HTML and CSS before displaying a page. Which account of DOM, CSSOM and the rendering pipeline is accurate?

choices.text: The DOM contains only visible nodes and the CSSOM contains final pixels; layout reconstructs the original markup.
The CSSOM computes element geometry before selectors are matched; the DOM then records rasterized pixels for paint.
The render tree contains every DOM node, including display:none content; styles are resolved only after the first paint.
The DOM represents markup and the CSSOM represents CSS; they inform the render tree before layout computes geometry.

questions.explanation: HTML parsing builds the DOM and CSS parsing builds the CSSOM. Together they inform styled renderable content; layout computes geometry, followed by painting and compositing. The render tree is not simply every DOM node: display:none content is excluded.

sources.title: Populating the page: how browsers work
sources.claim: HTML builds the DOM and CSS builds the CSSOM; they inform the render tree, layout computes geometry, and paint and compositing produce displayed output.

questions.prompt: An eligible transform animation runs smoothly while the main thread is busy. Which Chromium behavior explains this?

choices.text: The compositor still recalculates every element layout for each transform frame.
Smooth animation proves the compositor executes all JavaScript callbacks independently.
The compositor can update the effect without repeating layout and paint.
Every CSS animation automatically avoids main-thread work regardless of its property.

questions.explanation: Eligible transform effects can be composited without repeating layout and paint. Eligibility depends on the effect and circumstances; this does not move arbitrary JavaScript callbacks off the main thread.

sources.title: RenderingNG architecture
sources.claim: Chromium separates style, layout, paint, raster and compositing; eligible visual effects can skip earlier pipeline stages.

questions.prompt: A navigation response is a downloadable file rather than a document to display. Why might no renderer commit follow?

choices.text: Every download response must first be committed as a displayed document.
The browser can hand the response to download handling instead.
The browser checks whether a response is a download only after completing layout.
A download response is ordinary HTML rendering with painting disabled after parsing.

questions.explanation: Response handling can select download processing without committing a displayed document. Download classification is not a layout or paint decision.

sources.title: Inside look at modern web browser (part 2)
sources.claim: Navigation uses network requests, may follow redirects, checks response type and commits the document to a renderer.

questions.prompt: A dependency must execute before a classic script that uses it. Both are external. Which scheduling choice retains their document order without blocking parsing during download?

choices.text: Put the dependency first and use `defer` on both scripts.
Put the dependency first and use `async` on both scripts.
Put the dependency last and use `async` on both scripts.
Put the dependency last and use `defer` on both scripts.

questions.explanation: Defer keeps document order after parsing. Async does not guarantee order, and putting the dependency last with defer preserves the wrong order.

sources.title: HTML Standard: scripting
sources.claim: Classic script execution depends on async and defer; module scripts are deferred by default and async changes their scheduling.

questions.prompt: A teammate describes the navigation boundary. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A redirect must be committed as the final displayed document before it is followed.
A response marked for download must first create a displayed HTML document.
Redirects can require another network request.
A document commit transfers navigation to a renderer.
Every navigation response must be rendered as HTML.

questions.explanation: a: Following a redirect belongs to navigation, before a suitable final document commit. b: Download handling can consume the response without committing a new displayed document. c: The network handling follows a redirect destination. d: A suitable response is committed for document processing. e: Downloads and other response handling paths exist.

sources.title: Inside look at modern web browser (part 2)
sources.claim: Navigation uses network requests, may follow redirects, checks response type and commits the document to a renderer.

questions.prompt: A page mixes external classic and module scripts. Which scheduling claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Defer makes classic scripts block parsing during download.
A classic async script may run before parsing finishes.
Classic defer scripts retain their document order.
Module scripts block HTML parsing by default until their entire dependency graph executes.
Async guarantees execution in document order.

questions.explanation: a: The purpose is to defer execution instead of blocking parsing. b: Async scripts execute when ready. c: Deferred execution occurs in order after parsing. d: Module scripts are deferred by default rather than blocking parsing like ordinary classic scripts. e: Download readiness can change the execution order.

sources.title: HTML Standard: scripting
sources.claim: Classic script execution depends on async and defer; module scripts are deferred by default and async changes their scheduling.

questions.prompt: A developer interprets a Chromium rendering trace. Which stage descriptions hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Style computes CSS values for DOM content.
Layout calculates element sizes and positions.
Paint records a display list for drawing.
Raster computes selector matches and element geometry before building styles.
Compositing recomputes every DOM element layout on every displayed frame.

questions.explanation: a: The style stage creates computed styles. b: The layout stage creates geometry. c: Painting produces drawing instructions before raster. d: Style and layout produce styles and geometry; raster converts prepared drawing data into pixels. e: Compositing combines prepared visual artifacts and need not redo layout each frame.

sources.title: RenderingNG architecture
sources.claim: Chromium separates style, layout, paint, raster and compositing; eligible visual effects can skip earlier pipeline stages.

questions.prompt: A team plans animation work in Chromium. Which assumptions are sound? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Compositor work can be isolated from main-thread work.
Every visual change always runs every rendering stage.
Every transform animation qualifies for compositor-only execution regardless of circumstances.
Every CSS animation moves its JavaScript handlers onto the compositor thread.
Some visual effects can skip layout and paint.

questions.explanation: a: The separate compositor thread supports responsiveness. b: Stages may be skipped when not needed. c: Compositor eligibility depends on the effect and rendering conditions. d: Compositor effects do not move arbitrary JavaScript handlers off the main thread. e: The pipeline can omit stages when their output is reusable.

sources.title: RenderingNG architecture
sources.claim: Chromium separates style, layout, paint, raster and compositing; eligible visual effects can skip earlier pipeline stages.
